text: Agile is a popular way of managing projects, especially in software development. Instead of planning everything at once, teams work in short periods called sprints, usually lasting two to four weeks. Before each sprint, the team chooses tasks from a prioritised list called the backlog. These tasks are often written as user stories, which describe what a user needs from the product. Every day, the team holds a short meeting called a standup to share progress and discuss problems. This iterative approach allows teams to adapt quickly, improve the product step by step, and respond to feedback throughout the project.
